title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This page belongs to Grothendieck's preparatory notes (c. 1972) for what became the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture. The next page defines a connection of 'niveau zéro' (finite monodromy) and asks whether it forces finite monodromy over C. Here he works out the rank-one case completely, as a warm-up. For X of finite type over a field k (geometrically unibranch), a stratified invertible module L is called 'intégrable' if L^{⊗n} is trivial as a stratified module for some n>0 prime to p. Equivalently, its class has finite prime-to-p order in the group of stratified line bundles, i.e. finite monodromy of order prime to p.

(1) Characteristic 0, L = O_X.
- A flat connection on O_X is d+ω with ω a closed 1-form.
- Two such connections are isomorphic iff the forms differ by dlog u, with u in Γ(X,O_X^*).
- The connection d+ω is 'intégrable' iff nω = dlog u for some n and some unit u.
- By Rosenlicht's unit theorem, the group Λ = dlog Γ(X,O^*) ≅ Γ(O^*)/k^* is free of finite rank, Λ ≅ Z^r.
- So the isomorphism classes of integrable connections on O_X form ((1/n)-multiples of Λ)/Λ = Λ⊗Q/Z ≅ (Q/Z)^r. This is nonzero as soon as r>0: Kummer covers u^{1/n} give non-trivial connections on O_X with finite monodromy.
- If X is complete, or more generally if all global units are constant, every integrable connection on O_X is trivial. In other words, a 1-form that is locally a rational multiple of a logarithmic derivative is zero.

(2) Arbitrary characteristic, stratifications in the sense of Crystals/Dix exposés. Assume Γ(X,O_X)^* consists of horizontal functions, e.g. X proper and geometrically reduced. Claim: the only integrable stratification T on O_X is the trivial one. Proof:
- T^{⊗n} is trivial, so it has a nowhere-vanishing horizontal section σ.
- The section σ_0 = 1 satisfies σ_0^{⊗n} = λσ with λ a unit.
- λ is horizontal by hypothesis, so σ_0^{⊗n} is horizontal.
- Since n is prime to p, σ_0 itself is horizontal, so T is trivial.

Consequence. An integrable stratification on an invertible module is unique when it exists. So invertible modules with integrable stratification are classified exactly by line bundles L with L^{⊗n} ≅ O_X for some n>0 prime to p, i.e. prime-to-p torsion of Pic. This is the Kummer-theoretic description of rank-one, finite-order, prime-to-p characters of π_1, i.e. μ_n-torsors.
errors: Rosenlicht finiteness and the identification Γ(O^*)/k^* ≅ Z^r need k algebraically closed in Γ(X,O_X) (geometric integrality). Otherwise k^* should be replaced by the units of the algebraic closure of k in Γ(O_X). The note does not state this.

The step 'σ_0^n horizontal ⇒ σ_0 horizontal' for stratifications in char p is asserted without detail. It is correct for n prime to p (infinitesimal deformations of a unit with an n-th power fixed are trivial when n is invertible), but the argument is only sketched.
'X complète' implies constant units only with geometric reducedness/connectedness; Grothendieck corrects this himself by inserting the hypothesis 'Γ(X,O_X^*) formé de sections horizontales'.
Existence of an integrable stratification on any L with L^n ≅ O_X (n prime to p), via the μ_n-cover, is implicit rather than proved.

ideas.what: In char 0, connections on O_X with finite monodromy, modulo isomorphism, form Λ⊗Q/Z ≅ (Q/Z)^r, where Λ = dlog of global units ≅ Z^r (Rosenlicht).
ideas.modern_name: Rank-one local systems of finite order from Kummer covers / torsion in the group of rank-one flat connections

ideas.what: On a proper (geometrically reduced) X, the only finite-order prime-to-p stratification on O_X is trivial, so integrable stratified line bundles correspond exactly to prime-to-p torsion line bundles.
ideas.modern_name: Rank-one stratified bundles with finite monodromy = prime-to-p torsion in Pic (Kummer/μ_n-torsors)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gieseker (1975, flat bundles in char p); Kummer theory folklore

ideas.what: Definition of an 'integrable' (finite-monodromy) stratification as one whose tensor power, or pullback to a finite étale cover, is trivial; preparatory to the p-curvature question on the next page.
ideas.modern_name: Finite (essentially finite) stratified bundles; setting of the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (conjecture, via Katz 1972 'Algebraic solutions of differential equations'); Nori, dos Santos for finite bundles
ideas.where_published: Attributed to Grothendieck in Katz, Invent. Math. 18 (1972)

deep.surprise_reason: A routine rank-one warm-up, correct up to minor hypotheses. It is of historical interest as a working draft for the Grothendieck–Katz p-curvature conjecture (around 1972), but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: 'qui ne sont isomorphes à la connexion triviale' should read 'qui ne sont pas isomorphes à la connexion triviale'.
'[on fait le groupe' should read '[en fait le groupe'.

First line: '$\lambda$' is likely '$r$' (the rank): 'lorsque r n'est pas nul, il [L⊗Q] n'est pas identique au groupe des dérivées logarithmiques'. The phrase 'types de diviseurs multiples' likely means 'formes multiples (rationnels) de dérivées logarithmiques'.
The insertion '{+de Γ(X,O_X^*) formé de sections horizontales+}' is a marginal alternative hypothesis to 'complète': 'si Γ(X,O_X^*) est formé de sections horizontales'.
'$\mathcal{L}_X^{\otimes n}=\mathcal{O}_X$' is probably '$\mathcal{O}_X^{\otimes n}=\mathcal{O}_X$' (with stratification $T^{\otimes n}$).
'séparable sur k' is plausibly 'géométriquement réduit / séparable sur k'.
Final line: 'modules inversibles L tels que ∃ n>0, n premier à p, avec $L^{\otimes n}\simeq\mathcal{O}_X$'.
